findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the uploaded customer master spreadsheet) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS. Any data written here lacks key-managed encryption and the audit trail that KMS grants provide.

The bucket is explicitly annotated as public and has no ACL restriction and no accompanying aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so ACL or policy grants to AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers are not blocked. This bucket holds a customer master file, so anonymous read access would expose customer records.

No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects in this bucket may be retrieved over unencrypted HTTP. Combined with the sensitive customer object stored here, this permits interception of data in transit.

A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument, and the target bucket has no default encryption and no public access block. Sensitive customer data is therefore stored in cleartext in a bucket with weak access controls.
This bucket stores financial data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects are not encrypted with a managed KMS key at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so operational data is stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so data-science datasets are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption at rest, unlike the logs bucket in the same file.
